summary: The platform we developed translates NASA microgravity combustion data into an interactive fire-safety decision tool for spacecraft and habitats. Powered by a physics-informed machine learning pipeline, it predicts flame spread and extinction thresholds, enabling mission architects to test countermeasures—such as material substitution—to safeguard astronauts.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Our Flame in Freefall platform is an interactive decision-support tool that translates NASA microgravity combustion flight data into real-time fire safety insights. Built on curated datasets from orbital missions (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, ACME), it uses a physics-informed machine learning engine that calculates:

  • Oxygen Partial Pressure to evaluate the true chemical driving force in low-pressure, oxygen-enriched environments.
  • Forced Airflow Dynamics to account for low-flow radiative quenching and high-flow blowoff.
  • Unified Flame Classification across solids, droplets, and gas burners, using 200 bootstrap iterations to output rigorous 5th-to-95th percentile confidence bands.

Benefits & Impact

  • Dynamic Countermeasure Testing: Evaluates live mitigations in its Habitat check tool—e.g., on the ISS (19–23% O2), acrylic (PMMA) exhibits a 96% baseline flame spread risk, which drops to 24% by switching to Nomex, or to 86% by lowering O2 by 4%.
  • Evidence Grounding: Every prediction references the closest historical flight runs, providing empirical verification rather than black-box outputs.
  • Astronaut Life Safety: In isolated spacecraft and lunar/Martian bases, evacuation is impossible. Because buoyant convection vanishes in microgravity, spherical flames form and conventional smoke detectors lag. The tool equips mission architects to select safe materials and design resilient cabin atmospheres.
  • Terrestrial Impact: Fundamental microgravity combustion insights into cool flames directly inform improved fire suppression in confined spaces (submarines, aircraft).

Tools, Languages & Development

  • Stack: Python (data processing, feature physics, and ML pipeline using pandas, numpy, and scikit-learn) and TypeScript / HTML5 / CSS deployed on Vercel for client-side web inference.
  • AI Collaboration: Built with Claude (Anthropic) to develop the machine learning architecture and full-stack web integration.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered

  • Cross-Regime Physics Bridging: Solid materials borrow pressure response dynamics from Burning Rate Emulator (BRE) flight data, filling empirical gaps where low-pressure tests were sparse.
  • Microgravity Flammability Shifts: Materials ignite and sustain fire at lower oxygen concentrations in space than on Earth.
